```lean
/-- A renaming of identities (§49, last paragraph): a bijection of `Nat` with its inverse. -/
structure Ren where
  f : Nat → Nat
  g : Nat → Nat
  gf : ∀ i, g (f i) = i
  fg : ∀ i, f (g i) = i

def Ren.id : Ren := ⟨fun i => i, fun i => i, fun _ => rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩
def Ren.symm (π : Ren) : Ren := ⟨π.g, π.f, π.fg, π.gf⟩
def Ren.comp (π' π : Ren) : Ren :=
  ⟨fun i => π'.f (π.f i), fun i => π.g (π'.g i), fun i => by simp [π'.gf, π.gf],
   fun i => by simp [π'.fg, π.fg]⟩

/-- Renaming of a permutation `τ` of `List.range n`: old `x < n` goes to its position in `τ`,
new `i < n` comes from `τ[i]`; identity from `n` on. -/
def Ren.ofPerm (τ : List Nat) (n : Nat) (h : τ.Perm (List.range n)) : Ren where
  f x := if x < n then τ.idxOf x else x
  g i := if hi : i < τ.length then τ[i] else i
  gf := …   -- compiled, section 8
  fg := …

def Holder.ren (π : Ren) : Holder → Holder        -- §40, §42: frames are not renamed
  | .frame f => .frame f
  | .place p => .place (π.f p)

def Place.ren (π : Ren) (pl : Place) : Place := ⟨pl.parent.map π.f, pl.owner.ren π, pl.kind⟩

/-- Authorities related by the renaming; footprints up to permutation (§42: a set). -/
structure AuthRel (π α : Ren) (y y' : Authority) : Prop where
  mode : y'.mode = y.mode
  origin : y'.origin = y.origin.map α.f
  footprint : y'.footprint.Perm (y.footprint.map π.f)
  holder : y'.holder = y.holder.ren π
  active : y'.active = y.active

/-- Pinning obligations related by the renaming; identities kept (§74, §75). -/
structure PinRel (π : Ren) (ob ob' : PinOb) : Prop where
  place : ob'.place = π.f ob.place
  leaves : ob'.leaves.Perm (ob.leaves.map π.f)
  active : ob'.active = ob.active

/-- Place lists related by the renaming (§40); fresh identities fixed. -/
structure PRel (π : Ren) (P P' : List Place) : Prop where
  len : P'.length = P.length
  get : ∀ q, P'[π.f q]? = (P[q]?).map (Place.ren π)
  fix : ∀ q, P.length ≤ q → π.f q = q

/-- States related by place renaming `π` and authority renaming `α` (§38, §49 last paragraph);
footprints, anchors (§44: a set) and pinned leaves up to permutation. -/
structure SRel (π α : Ren) (s s' : S3) : Prop where
  F : s'.F = s.F
  nF : s'.nF = s.nF
  P : PRel π s.P s'.P
  I : ∀ l, s'.I (π.f l) = s.I l
  Alen : s'.A.length = s.A.length
  A : ∀ x, Option.Rel (AuthRel π α) (s.A[x]?) (s'.A[α.f x]?)
  Afix : ∀ x, s.A.length ≤ x → α.f x = x
  D : ∀ q, (s'.D (π.f q)).Perm ((s.D q).map α.f)
  dead : ∀ q, s'.dead (π.f q) = s.dead q
  pins : ∀ o : Nat, Option.Rel (PinRel π) (s.pins[o]?) (s'.pins[o]?)

/-- Parent and origin links go to smaller identities (§49.2, §49.5; representation of
acyclicity, §49 last paragraph). -/
def DownP (P : List Place) : Prop := ∀ j o, parentOf P j = some o → o < j
def DownA (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ j o, s.org j = some o → o < j
def Down (s : S3) : Prop := DownP s.P ∧ DownA s

/-- `π` keeps the order of the parts of every place, their positional field order (§63.2). -/
def SibMono (π : Ren) (P : List Place) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y p, parentOf P x = some p → parentOf P y = some p → x < y → π.f x < π.f y

/-- The simulation invariant. -/
structure Sim (π α : Ren) (s s' : S3) : Prop where
  rel : SRel π α s s'
  down : Down s
  down' : Down s'
  sib : SibMono π s.P

/-- Owner-accepted hypothesis (2026-11-06): `Satisfiable` (§71) does not distinguish states equal
up to permutation of footprint, anchor and pin-leaf lists (§42, §44). -/
def KExt (k : K) : Prop :=
  ∀ p sh s t, SRel Ren.id Ren.id s t → k.Satisfiable p sh s → k.Satisfiable p sh t

/-- The contract renamed (§48, §80); `FreeCompat`'s `auth` is opaque (§70.2); obligations keep
their identities (§75). -/
def K.rename (π α : Ren) (k : K) : K where
  DeclaredDisjoint r r' := k.DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.g) (r'.map π.g)
  SharedMutable l := k.SharedMutable (π.g l)
  Pinned l := k.Pinned (π.g l)
  ExternalDone o := k.ExternalDone o
  Deallocable p := k.Deallocable (π.g p)
  FreeCompat p a := k.FreeCompat (π.g p) a
  Satisfiable p sh t := ∃ t₀, SRel π α t₀ t ∧ k.Satisfiable (π.g p) sh t₀

/-- Contracts corresponding under the renaming, `Satisfiable` excepted (§48). -/
structure KCorr (π α : Ren) (k k' : K) : Prop where
  dd : ∀ r r', k'.DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.f) (r'.map π.f) ↔ k.DeclaredDisjoint r r'
  shared : ∀ l, k'.SharedMutable (π.f l) ↔ k.SharedMutable l
  pinned : ∀ l, k'.Pinned (π.f l) ↔ k.Pinned l
  done : ∀ o, k'.ExternalDone o ↔ k.ExternalDone o
  dealloc : ∀ p, k'.Deallocable (π.f p) ↔ k.Deallocable p
  compat : ∀ p a, k'.FreeCompat (π.f p) a ↔ k.FreeCompat p a

/-- Outcomes related by the renaming (§58). -/
def OutRel (π α : Ren) : Outcome3 S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop
  | .ok t, .ok t' => SRel π α t t'
  | .reject, .reject => True
  | .fail, .fail => True
  | _, _ => False

/-- Outcome relations corresponding in both directions (§58). -/
def StepCorr (π α : Ren) (R R' : Outcome3 S3 → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ o, R o → ∃ o', R' o' ∧ OutRel π α o o') ∧ ∀ o', R' o' → ∃ o, R o ∧ OutRel π α o o'

/-- Arguments renamed (§60–§75). Shapes are not renamed (§71.1, §72.2: fresh parents); `auth` is
opaque (§70.2); `o` is an obligation identity (§75). -/
def KernelOp.ren (π α : Ren) : KernelOp → KernelOp
  | .derive src region m => .derive (α.f src) (region.map π.f) m
  | .split src rs => .split (α.f src) (rs.map (·.map π.f))
  | .release a => .release (α.f a)
  | .transfer src dst => .transfer (π.f src) (π.f dst)
  | .depend q x => .depend (π.f q) (α.f x)
  | .enter ps ls => .enter (ps.map α.f) ls
  | .exit => .exit
  | .read a ls => .read (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .write a ls => .write (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .writeShared a ls => .writeShared (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .pin p => .pin (π.f p)
  | .unpin o => .unpin o
  | .endUse p => .endUse (π.f p)
  | .free p auth => .free (π.f p) auth
  | .alloc pr ow ls => .alloc (π.f pr) (π.f ow) ls
  | .store a p => .store (α.f a) (π.f p)

/-- A run (§57, §58): verdicts in order; `ok` continues from its state, `reject` and `fail` from
the unchanged state. -/
inductive Run (k : K) : S3 → List KernelOp → List (Outcome3 Unit) → S3 → Prop
  | nil {s : S3} : Run k s [] [] s
  | ok {s t u : S3} {op : KernelOp} {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} :
      op.Step k s (.ok t) → Run k t ops vs u → Run k s (op :: ops) (.ok () :: vs) u
  | reject {s u : S3} {op : KernelOp} {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} :
      op.Step k s .reject → Run k s ops vs u → Run k s (op :: ops) (.reject :: vs) u
  | fail {s u : S3} {op : KernelOp} {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} :
      op.Step k s .fail → Run k s ops vs u → Run k s (op :: ops) (.fail :: vs) u

/-- Two `StaticsOK` numberings of one declaration (§47; §49 last paragraph; §63.2). -/
structure Renumbered (statics : Statics) (σ : List Nat) : Prop where
  perm : σ.Perm (List.range statics.length)
  cons : ConsistentRenumbering σ statics
  ok : StaticsOK statics
  ok' : StaticsOK (renumber σ statics)

def Renumbered.π (h : Renumbered statics σ) : Ren := Ren.ofPerm σ statics.length h.perm

/-- New root authority `j'` holds the root of new root static `R'[j']`, whose old index is
`π.g R'[j']`, at old position `R.idxOf (π.g R'[j'])` (§47). -/
def rootPerm (statics : Statics) (σ : List Nat) (π : Ren) : List Nat :=
  (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).map fun i' =>
    (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).idxOf (π.g i')

def Renumbered.α (h : Renumbered statics σ) : Ren :=
  Ren.ofPerm (rootPerm statics σ h.π) _ h.rootPerm_perm
```

Conventions for every statement below: implicit `{π α : Ren} {s s' : S3} {k k' : K}`;
`h : SRel π α s s'`, `hd : Down s`, `hd' : Down s'`, `hS : Sim π α s s'`,
`hK : KCorr π α k k'`; for place lists `hP : PRel π P P'`, `hdP : DownP P`, `hdP' : DownP P'`,
`hs : SibMono π P`. "f-form" is `π.f l ∈ L' ↔ l ∈ L`; the "g-form" `l' ∈ L' ↔ π.g l' ∈ L` follows
by `Ren.mem_iff_g` (below). Every iff is proved forward and closed by symmetry.

## 7. Risks: where a verdict could differ between two numberings

| # | Construct | Failure | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | `kids`, `posIn`, `corr` (§63.2, `transfer`) | Positions in index-ordered children. A renaming that reverses fields changes `corr`, hence holders and owners after `transfer`. Checked with the corpus runner: `st1` = src 0 {1,2} Init, dst 3 {4,5}, static 6 owned by static 1; `σ = swap 4 5` maps `st1` to itself (both numberings `StaticsOK`) but breaks `field_order`. `[transfer 0 3, endUse 4, pin 6]` gives `[ok, ok, reject]`; the renamed `[transfer 0 3, endUse 5, pin 6]` gives `[ok, ok, ok]`. | `ConsistentRenumbering.field_order` gives `SibMono` at init; `Sim.sib` carries it; appended places keep it (`shapeP_sib`); `kids_ren`, `corr_ren` (compiled). |
| R2 | `chainF` (`o < i`), `corrF` (`p < r`), fuel = index | Truncation on a non-downward link; `SRel` does not transport link order (`π` not monotone). | `Down s` and `Down s'` in `Sim`, from `init_kinv` on both numberings, preserved per step on each side (`op_down`, no `DDSound`). Effect states read by preconditions get `XEff_down` from `Down s` (enter: under `localsOK`). Fuel handled by `chain_cons`, `corr_step` (existing, through `chainF_fuel`, `corrF_fuel`). |
| R3 | Footprint lists of root authorities (`S3.init`, `enterEff`, `allocEff`) and of pin obligations (`pinEff`) | Built by `filter` over `List.range`: their order depends on the numbering. Example: root R with fields A {a1} and b; numbered `[R, A, b, a1]` the list is `[b, a1]`, numbered `[R, A, a1, b]` it is `[a1, b]`. | `Perm` in `AuthRel.footprint`, `PinRel.leaves`. Every consumer reads membership only: `effective`, `descModes`, `afp`, `DerivePre`, `SplitPre`, `ActiveDerivedOutside`, `SelfLock`, `StorePre.noCover`, `IsRootOf`, `EndUseAccessOK`, `FreeAccessOK`, `FreeAnchorOK`, `freeS`, `S3.pin` (`contains`), `CoversHolder`, `WF3`, `RootChain`, `RootHeld`, `I1`, `I2`, `NoDangling`. A future definition reading these lists by position would break the relation. |
| R4 | `D` after `transfer` (`movedTo`: `flatMap` over places in index order) | Order of anchors differs. | `Perm` in `SRel.D`. Consumers: `∈` (`I3`, `ReleasePre`, `ExitPre`, `EndUsePre`, `FreePre`, `AnchorOrder`, `movedDeps`), `filter` (`releaseEff`), `map` (`exitEff`), `++` (`dependEff`, `storeEff`, `transferEff`), `flatMap` (`movedTo`, `movedDeps`): all `Perm`-compatible. |
| R5 | `descModes` (`filterMap` over `List.range |A|`) | Mode list order differs. | `effOf` reads `= []` and `∈` only: `effOf_congr`. |
| R6 | Root authority identities in `S3.init` (`rootIdx` order) | Root of a static gets a different index. | `α` built from `rootPerm`; `rootIdx_α`. |
| R7 | `K.Satisfiable` reads the whole state (§71) | A contract reading list order (e.g. `s.A[0]?.map (·.footprint) = some [2, 3]`) gives `ok` in one numbering and `fail` in the other (R3 example). | `k.rename` evaluates `k` on numbering-1 states related to `s'` (absorbs `π`, `α`); `KExt k` (owner-accepted) absorbs list permutations. Only the backward direction of `satisfiable_ren` uses `KExt`. |
| R8 | `DeclaredDisjoint` reads lists | Order of a region could matter. | Regions are `split` arguments, renamed elementwise in order: exact, no extensionality. |
| R9 | `FreeCompat p auth` | If `auth` were an authority identity, it would need `α`. | §70.2: "this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel": not renamed. |
| R10 | `ExternalDone o`, `unpin o` (§75) | Obligation identities. | Same append order on both sides; not renamed; `SRel.pins` indexwise. |
| R11 | Shapes of `enter`, `alloc`, and `Satisfiable`'s `sh` | Parents are place identities. | `ShapeOK |P| ls` forces parents and owning elements `≥ |P|`, fixed by `π`; `ShapeOK` depends only on `|P|` and `ls`. Not renamed. |

theorem chain_ren {org org' : Nat → Option Nat} {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hd : ∀ j o, org j = some o → o < j) (hd' : ∀ j o, org' j = some o → o < j)
    (h : ∀ j, org' (f j) = (org j).map f) : ∀ i, chain org' (f i) = (chain org i).map f := by
  intro i
  induction i using Nat.strongRecOn with
  | _ i ih =>
    cases ho : org i with
    | none => rw [chain_none ho, chain_none (by rw [h, ho]; rfl)]; rfl
    | some o =>
      have h' : org' (f i) = some (f o) := by rw [h, ho]; rfl
      rw [chain_cons ho (hd _ _ ho), chain_cons h' (hd' _ _ h'), ih o (hd _ _ ho)]
      rfl

theorem eq_of_sorted_mem {l l' : List Nat} (h : l.Pairwise (· < ·)) (h' : l'.Pairwise (· < ·))
    (hm : ∀ a, a ∈ l ↔ a ∈ l') : l = l' :=
  List.Perm.eq_of_pairwise (le := (· < ·))
    (fun a b _ _ hab hba => absurd (Nat.lt_trans hab hba) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)) h h'
    ((List.perm_ext_iff_of_nodup (h.imp Nat.ne_of_lt) (h'.imp Nat.ne_of_lt)).2 hm)

theorem kids_ren {π : Ren} {P P' : List Place} (h : PRel π P P') (hs : SibMono π P) (x : Nat) :
    kids P' (π.f x) = (kids P x).map π.f := by
  apply eq_of_sorted_mem (kids_sorted P' _)
  · rw [List.pairwise_map]
    refine (kids_sorted P x).imp_of_mem fun {a b} ha hb hab => ?_
    exact hs a b x (mem_kids.1 ha).2 (mem_kids.1 hb).2 hab
  · intro a
    rw [← π.fg a]
    simp only [mem_kids, List.mem_map, h.lt_iff, h.parentOf, Ren.f_inj]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      refine ⟨π.g a, ⟨h1, ?_⟩, rfl⟩
      cases e : parentOf P (π.g a) with
      | none => rw [e] at h2; cases h2
      | some p =>
        rw [e] at h2; simp only [Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq, Ren.f_inj] at h2; rw [h2]
    · rintro ⟨b, ⟨hb1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩

content.text:
La conception de la bisimulation pour StaticsOK (b) est terminée, et la recherche de contre-exemple n'en a trouvé aucun.

**Recherche de contre-exemple.** Elle a parcouru environ 500 000 paires d'opérations sur des exécutions aléatoires et ciblées, avec une vraie permutation des statiques et des autorités racines, sans aucune différence de verdict ni d'état. J'ai aussi vérifié que chaque hypothèse est nécessaire : quand on en retire une, un écart apparaît.
- **Ordre des champs** : sans lui, un `transfer` est `ok` d'un côté et `reject` de l'autre.
- **StaticsOK sur les deux numérotations** : sans lui, les chaînes sont tronquées.
- **K extensionnel** : un `Satisfiable` qui lit l'ordre d'une empreinte donne `ok` contre `fail`.

**Choix de conception que vous verrez dans le code :**
- Les états sont reliés à permutation près (`List.Perm`) des empreintes, des ancres et des feuilles épinglées. L'égalité exacte est fausse dès l'état initial, car l'ordre des feuilles d'une empreinte dépend de la numérotation.
- L'hypothèse sur `Satisfiable` est donc exactement « invariant par permutation de ces listes », celle que vous avez acceptée. Elle sert dans un seul sens de la preuve, pour `alloc`.
- Dans le K renommé, l'argument `auth` de `FreeCompat` n'est pas renommé, puisque §70.2 le dit opaque pour le noyau. Les identités d'obligation d'`ExternalDone` (§75) ne le sont pas non plus.

**Où en est l'implémentation.** Le travail est découpé en dix fichiers sous `Access/Rename/`. Un agent écrit en ce moment la fondation : renommages, relation d'états, et lemmes sur les places et les notions dérivées. Ensuite viendront six tâches en parallèle (les opérations par groupes, le transport de KInv et I5, l'état initial), puis l'assemblage : correspondance des verdicts par exécution et de l'atteignabilité dans les deux sens.

PR ernlang/ern#2 est revenue en draft. Les cinq commits sur les autres points sont en local et ne sont pas encore poussés.

356 rename-foundation-api.md
### 4.2 Ops.lean of the kernel

Each operation file exports, per operation X, `XPre_ren` (iff), `XEff_ren` (`SRel` of the
effects), `XEff_down` where the effect changes links, and `X_corr` (the `StepCorr` of the two
step relations, from `guarded_corr`), all specialised in `X_corr` to `k' = k.rename π α` via
`KCorr.rename`.

| Definition | Kind | Lemma |
|---|---|---|
| `mapI` | index-based | `getElem?_mapI` (existing) |
| `deriveEff` | fresh | `deriveEff_ren h src region m : SRel π α (deriveEff s src region m) (deriveEff s' (α.f src) (region.map π.f) m)`; `deriveEff_down hd (hsrc : src < s.A.length)` |
| `DerivePre` | range, chain | `derivePre_ren hS src region m : DerivePre s' (α.f src) (region.map π.f) m ↔ DerivePre s src region m` |
| `splitEff` | fresh | `splitEff_ren h src rs : SRel π α (splitEff s src rs) (splitEff s' (α.f src) (rs.map (·.map π.f)))`; `splitEff_down hd hsrc` |
| `DistribExcl` | chain | `SRel.distribExcl h hd hd' src j p : DistribExcl s' (α.f src) (α.f j) (π.f p) ↔ DistribExcl s src j p` |
| `SplitPre` | K (exact lists), range | `splitPre_ren hK hS src rs : SplitPre k' s' (α.f src) (rs.map (·.map π.f)) ↔ SplitPre k s src rs` (`List.pairwise_map`) |
| `releaseEff` | idx | `releaseEff_ren h a : SRel π α (releaseEff s a) (releaseEff s' (α.f a))` (`D`: `filter` of `map` with `α` injective); `releaseEff_down hd` |
| `HolderRight` | — | `SRel.holderRight h hd hd' o : HolderRight s' (o.ren π) ↔ HolderRight s o` |
| `ReleasePre` | range, chain | `releasePre_ren hS a : ReleasePre s' (α.f a) ↔ ReleasePre s a` |
| `kids` | pos | `kids_ren hP hs x : kids P' (π.f x) = (kids P x).map π.f` (compiled; `List.Perm.eq_of_pairwise`) |
| `posIn` | pos | `posIn_map (hf : ∀ i j, f i = f j → i = j) r l : posIn (f r) (l.map f) = posIn r l` (compiled) |
| `corrF`, `corr` | chain (fuel = index, `p < r`), pos | `corr_ren hP hdP hdP' hs src dst : ∀ r, corr P' (π.f src) (π.f dst) (π.f r) = (corr P src dst r).map π.f` (compiled, with `corr_none`) |

  ```lean
theorem Sim.run_back (hk) (hS) (hr : Run (k.rename π α) s' (ops.map (KernelOp.ren π α)) vs u') :
    ∃ u, Run k s ops vs u ∧ Sim π α u u'
theorem Sim.run_back_any (hk) (hS) (hr : Run (k.rename π α) s' ops' vs u') :
    ∃ u, Run k s (ops'.map (KernelOp.ren π.symm α.symm)) vs u ∧ Sim π α u u'
theorem Renumbered.run (hk : KExt k) (h : Renumbered statics σ) (hr : Run k (S3.init statics) ops vs u) :
    ∃ u', Run (k.rename h.π h.α) (S3.init (renumber σ statics)) (ops.map (KernelOp.ren h.π h.α)) vs u'
      ∧ Sim h.π h.α u u'
theorem Renumbered.run_back (hk) (h) (hr : Run (k.rename h.π h.α) (S3.init (renumber σ statics))
    (ops.map (KernelOp.ren h.π h.α)) vs u') : ∃ u, Run k (S3.init statics) ops vs u ∧ Sim h.π h.α u u'
theorem Renumbered.reachable (hk) (h) (hs : Reachable k statics s) :
    ∃ s', Reachable (k.rename h.π h.α) (renumber σ statics) s' ∧ Sim h.π h.α s s'
theorem Renumbered.reachable_back (hk) (h) (hs' : Reachable (k.rename h.π h.α) (renumber σ statics) s') :
    ∃ s, Reachable k statics s ∧ Sim h.π h.α s s'
theorem Renumbered.properties (hk : KExt k) (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
    (DDSound (k.rename h.π h.α) ↔ DDSound k) ∧
    ((∀ s, Reachable k statics s → KInv s ∧ I5 k s) ↔

    (hp₁ : σ₁.Perm (List.range C.length)) (hc₁ : ConsistentRenumbering σ₁ C)
    (hok₁ : StaticsOK (renumber σ₁ C)) (hp₂ : σ₂.Perm (List.range C.length))
    (hc₂ : ConsistentRenumbering σ₂ C) (hok₂ : StaticsOK (renumber σ₂ C)) :
    ∃ τ, Renumbered (renumber σ₁ C) τ ∧ renumber τ (renumber σ₁ C) = renumber σ₂ C
  ```

  - The entry clause of `ConsistentRenumbering τ` holds for any permutation.
  - The equation also holds for references at or beyond `C.length`, because `idxOf` sends them all to `C.length`.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: axcheck.sh Module.Name [Module.Name ...]   (run after lake build of those modules)

La bisimulation de StaticsOK (b) est entièrement prouvée. Elle n'est pas encore commitée : j'attends le résultat d'une relecture adversariale de ses énoncés avant de commiter et de pousser.

**Ce qui est démontré.** Prenons deux numérotations StaticsOK d'une même déclaration, reliées par un renommage cohérent qui garde les parents, les propriétaires, les genres, les états initiaux et l'ordre des champs.
- **Verdicts identiques** : chaque exécution O1–O16, avec arguments renommés, donne les mêmes verdicts (`ok`, `reject` et `fail` confondus) et des états qui se correspondent. C'est `Renumbered.run` et `run_back`, qui reposent sur `op_corr` pour chaque opération.
- **Atteignabilité** : elle se correspond dans les deux sens (`Renumbered.reachable` et `reachable_back`).
- **Propriétés** : KInv et I5 se transportent. `Renumbered.properties` en conclut que les propriétés prouvées sur les états atteignables sont les mêmes pour les deux numérotations, et que `DDSound` est invariant.
- **Lien avec (a)** : deux numérotations quelconques obtenues par (a) sont toujours reliées ainsi (`renumber_renumbered`). Le choix de numérotation ne change donc rien.

**Vérifications.**
- Le build complet passe, en 40 jobs, sans avertissement.
- La recherche de `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` et `native_decide` ne trouve rien.
- Le relevé des axiomes porte sur les 37 modules. Rien n'y sort de `propext`, `Quot.sound` et `Classical.choice`, et ce dernier n'apparaît que dans `Statics` et `Rename/*`.
- Les exemples ne sont pas vides de sens : une déclaration où les places et les autorités racines sont vraiment permutées, et `KExt` satisfait par le contrat d'exemple.

**Deux choix de modélisation à connaître.**
- **États reliés à permutation près.** Les états se correspondent à permutation près des listes d'empreintes, d'ancres et de feuilles épinglées, que §42 et §44 traitent comme des ensembles. Cela tient à votre hypothèse `KExt`, qui ne sert que pour `alloc`, et dans un seul sens.
- **Suite d'une exécution après un `reject`.** Pour énoncer « mêmes verdicts », une exécution continue après un `reject` depuis l'état inchangé, comme après un `fail`. §58 ne dit rien de ce qui suit un `reject`. Never use an unquoted heredoc for Lean or docstrings: backticks run as shell commands; use `<<'EOF'` and pass paths by environment variable. `example`s escape a `collectAxioms` sweep: rename them to theorems in a scratch copy to check their axioms. `awk length` counts bytes, not characters: count line length in Python. Each check round finds errors in the previous round's wording: when a sentence is fixed in a docstring, grep the report for the same claim; quote arbitrages exactly (L2 said "hypothèse des énoncés", not "hors langage"); classify every item a deliverable asks to classify instead of moving it aside; a summary must not present a hypothesis restated in a conclusion as a result. Count theorem constants with internal ones (`isInternal`) and say which count you give. A callee cannot move a value out of a parameter's footprint (`ActiveDerivedOutside` counts the parameter itself): build values to transfer as callee locals. Authority ids shift with every alloc/issue/split: check them with `#eval` of `prun` prefixes before writing a case. A literal invariant from the material can fail under the full kernel extension: keep the literal statement with counterexamples and prove the parts that hold, under their own names. A runner's fallback state must be unreachable (e.g. no frame) or a statement "the run's state is reached" is vacuous when the run fails; give a lemma deriving success from reachability. Projecting `.2` out of an existential passes the elaborator but fails in the kernel: use `obtain`. When `step_ok_of`-style lemmas time out at `whnf`, pass the contract `k` and statics explicitly. Jalon 3 took four check rounds (11/9/9/4 confirmed): each round's fixes need their own narrow check. The list `Sublist` notation `<+` is scoped: write `List.Sublist`; `List.take_add` pulls `Classical.choice`. `omit … in` goes before the docstring. A `def` in a `variable (k : K)` section takes `k` only if it uses it: check call sites. In a multi-line `{ st with … }`, put each field on its own line at one column. Theorems stated for registered arenas (`ar ∈ s.arenas`) do not carry over to library instances: never cite them for one. Before writing "the only effect of X is Y", look for a witness in the other direction (derivability: the missing guard also turned a `fail` into an `ok`).

- Pour énoncer « mêmes verdicts », une exécution continue après un `reject` depuis l'état inchangé. C'est un choix de modélisation et la docstring le dit : §58 ne décrit rien après un `reject`.

  /-- §76.2: `internal` exists, with own mode `Modify` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/

  /-- §76.3: `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/
  fpEq : ∀ l, l ∈ s.afp sh.internal ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage
  /-- §40, §49.2: the storage has a leaf (HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/
  storageLeaf : ∃ l, l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage
  /-- §40, §49.2: every slot has a leaf (HandlePool v0.5, D.1). -/
  slotLeaf : ∀ q ∈ sh.places, ∃ l, l ∈ footprint s.P q
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.1: slots lie in the storage. -/
  slotIn : ∀ q ∈ sh.places, ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.1: slots are pairwise disjoint. -/
  disjoint : ∀ (a b qa qb : Nat), sh.places[a]? = some qa → sh.places[b]? = some qb → a ≠ b →
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P qa, l ∉ footprint s.P qb

of `shs` with its `internal`; the companion is younger than `internal`, of the mode of the
resolution, over the footprint of the storage; each entry authority is younger than the companion,

  ∃ sh ∈ shs, sh.id = r.pool ∧ sh.internal = r.internal ∧ r.internal < r.comp ∧

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main

/-!
# Access kernel: source leaves after an accepted `transfer` (§63.4, decision Q17)

Owner decision Q17 (validated 2026-11-06): the exemption of §63.4, for "the exercisable authority
on which that right rests and its origin chain", is accepted, and it is to be proved, on reachable
states, that (a) after an accepted `transfer` no active authority outside the grounding chain covers
the source leaves, and (b) every access of the grounding chain to these leaves is rejected. With `g`
any authority grounding the `Modify` right over `source` (`Grounds`, §43) and the grounding chain
`RightChain s g` (§63.4), after an accepted `transfer` (§63) from a reachable state (§57):

* (a) is proved: every active authority covering a source leaf lies in the grounding chain (§43,
  §50);
* (b) is proved for reads and for strict ancestors: a read (O9, §66) of a source leaf is rejected
  through every authority, the leaf being `Moved` (§41, §63 `ok` effect, §63.3 disjointness); a
  write (O10, §67) or a shared write (O11, §68) of a source leaf through a strict origin-chain
  ancestor of `g` is rejected, `g` being an active `Modify` descendant covering the leaf (§43
  case 3);
* (b) is false for O10 and O11 through `g` itself: a write or shared write of a source leaf through
  `g` is accepted in a reachable run (`TransferSourceWitness.write_through_ground_accepted`), since
  §67 and §68 have no `Init` precondition and `Moved` forbids reads only (§41, §53). This part is
  left to the owner.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- The grounding chain is unchanged by a transfer, which keeps every origin (§63 `ok` effect: no
authority is created or duplicated; §63.4). -/
theorem transfer_rightChain (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    RightChain (transferEff s src dst) = RightChain s := by
  funext g j; simp only [RightChain, (transfer_skel s src dst).ancs]
59-  · rfl
60-
61-/-- Core of Q17 (a) (decision Q17, validated 2026-11-06; §63.4, §43, §50): under `I1`, if `g`
62-grounds the `Modify` right over `q`, every active authority covering a leaf of `q` is `g` or an
63-origin-chain ancestor of `g`. A strict descendant of `g` covering the leaf would take away the
64-effective `Modify` of `g` (§43 cases 3–4); an unrelated one would contradict `I1` (§50). -/
65:theorem grounds_cover_rightChain {s : S3} (h1 : I1 s) {q g : Nat} (hg : Grounds s .modify q g)
66-    {x : Nat} {y : Authority} (hy : s.A[x]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) {l : Nat}
67-    (hl : l ∈ y.footprint) (hlq : l ∈ footprint s.P q) : RightChain s g x := by
68-  obtain ⟨z, hz, za, zl, zm, h0⟩ := allows_modify (hg.2.2 l hlq)
/-- Decision Q17 (validated 2026-11-06) on reachable states (§57; §63.4, §43, §50, §66–§68): for
a state reachable under `DDSound` (§80) from well-formed statics (§47), an accepted `transfer` of
`src`, and every authority `g` grounding the `Modify` right over `src` before the step:
(a) every authority active after the step covering a source leaf belongs to the grounding chain of
`g`; (b) for every list `ls` containing a source leaf, a read is rejected through every authority,
and a write or shared write is rejected through every strict origin-chain ancestor of `g`. This is
(b) of the decision without O10 and O11 through `g` itself, for which (b) is false:
`TransferSourceWitness.write_through_ground_accepted`. -/
theorem transfer_source_q17 {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s s' : S3} {src dst g : Nat}
    (hdd : DDSound k) (hst : StaticsOK statics) (hr : Reachable k statics s)
    (ht : TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s')) (hg : Grounds s .modify src g) :
    (∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s'.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
      l ∈ y.footprint → l ∈ footprint s'.P src → RightChain s' g x) ∧
    ∀ (ls : List Nat) (l : Nat), l ∈ ls → l ∈ footprint s'.P src →
      (∀ (a : Nat) (o : Outcome3 S3), Read3Step a ls s' o → o = .reject) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ s'.ancs g, ∀ o : Outcome3 S3, Write3Step x ls s' o → o = .reject) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ s'.ancs g, ∀ o : Outcome3 S3, WriteSharedStep k x ls s' o → o = .reject) :=
  ⟨transfer_source_cover_chain_of_i1 (reachable_kinv hdd hst hr).2.1.1.1 ht hg,
   fun _ _ hls hl => ⟨fun a _ h => transfer_source_read_rejected ht hl hls a h,
    fun _ hx _ h => transfer_source_anc_write_rejected ht hg hl hls hx h,
    fun _ hx _ h => transfer_source_anc_writeShared_rejected ht hg hl hls hx h⟩⟩

namespace TransferSourceWitness

open Examples

/-- The state after `transfer(0, 1)` from `S3.init st` (§47, §63 `ok` effect): leaf 0 `Moved`,
leaf 1 `Init`. -/
def t1 : S3 := transferEff s0 0 1

/-- Writes through the grounding authority itself are accepted on a moved source leaf (decision
Q17, validated 2026-11-06; §63.4, §67, §68, §41, §53): under `K0` (`DDSound`, §80) and the
well-formed statics `st` (§47), `S3.init st` is reachable, `transfer(0, 1)` is accepted, root
authority 0 grounds the `Modify` right over place 0, leaf 0 is a `Moved` source leaf afterwards,
and both a write (O10) and a shared write (O11) of leaf 0 through authority 0 are accepted, the
resulting state being reachable. Statement (b) of Q17 therefore fails for O10 and O11 through the
grounding authority itself. -/
theorem write_through_ground_accepted : DDSound K0 ∧ StaticsOK st ∧ Reachable K0 st s0 ∧
    TransferStep K0 0 1 s0 (.ok t1) ∧ Grounds s0 .modify 0 0 ∧ 0 ∈ footprint t1.P 0 ∧
    t1.I 0 = .moved ∧ Write3Step 0 [0] t1 (.ok (write3Eff t1 [0])) ∧
    WriteSharedStep K0 0 [0] t1 (.ok (write3Eff t1 [0])) ∧
    Reachable K0 st (write3Eff t1 [0]) := by
  have ht : TransferStep K0 0 1 s0 (.ok t1) := .ok (by decide)
  have hw : Write3Step 0 [0] t1 (.ok (write3Eff t1 [0])) := .ok (by decide)
  exact ⟨fun _ _ h => h.elim, by decide, .init, ht, by decide, by decide, by decide, hw,
    .ok (by decide), .step (.step .init (.transfer ht)) (.write hw)⟩

end TransferSourceWitness

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

p='Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Rename/Basic.lean'; s=open(p).read()
old='''/-- Owner-accepted hypothesis of 2026-11-06 on `Satisfiable` (§71, §48; §49, last paragraph): it
does not distinguish states equal up to permutation of footprint, anchor and pin-leaf lists
(§42, §44). -/'''
new='''/-- Interface obligation on the contract `K`, attached to §42 (the `footprint` of an authority is a
set; likewise the anchors `D(p)`, §44, and the leaves of a pinning obligation, §74): `Satisfiable`
(§71) does not distinguish states equal up to permutation of footprint, anchor and pin-leaf lists,
which the formalization represents as lists (§49, last paragraph). `K` is a parameter of the
formalization (§48, §80), not a concrete definition, so this is a hypothesis on it (accepted by the
owner on 2026-11-06), satisfied for instance by `Examples.K0` (`MainExamples.k0_ext`). Only the
renaming bisimulation depends on it: `satisfiable_ren` and `alloc_corr` (OpsEndFree), then
`op_corr`, `Sim.step`, `Sim.step_back`, `Sim.run`, `Sim.run_back`, `Sim.run_back_any`,
`Renumbered.run`, `Renumbered.run_back`, `Renumbered.reachable`, `Renumbered.reachable_back` and
`Renumbered.properties` (Main). -/'''
assert s.count(old)==1; open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new))
EOF

Quatre des cinq points sont faits en local. Rien n'est commité ni poussé pour l'instant.

1. **Q17 (b) reformulé.** L'en-tête de `TransferSource` et la docstring de `transfer_source_q17` donnent maintenant votre énoncé : toute lecture d'une feuille source est rejetée, tout accès par un ancêtre strict de l'autorité fondatrice est rejeté, et une écriture par l'autorité fondatrice est permise. Les preuves existantes n'ont pas changé. `write_through_ground_accepted` est conservé comme témoin positif.
2. **W2.** Le MISMATCH est supprimé et la propriété attendue suit le nouvel énoncé. Dans la description de la PR, la ligne W2 du tableau précise que le premier énoncé de (b) était erroné.
3. **`KExt`.** `K` est un paramètre et non une définition concrète : c'est une structure de prédicats (§48, §80), sur laquelle chaque théorème quantifie. `KExt` est donc documenté comme une obligation d'interface rattachée à §42 (et à §44 et §74 pour les ancres et les feuilles épinglées), avec un exemple qui la satisfait (`k0_ext`). Sa docstring liste les théorèmes qui en dépendent :
   - `satisfiable_ren` et `alloc_corr` ;
   - à travers eux, `op_corr`, `Sim.step`/`step_back`, `Sim.run`/`run_back`/`run_back_any` et `Renumbered.run`/`run_back`/`reachable`/`reachable_back`/`properties`.

   Aucun autre théorème de la formalisation n'en dépend.
5. **Redondance de §63.4.** Nouveau théorème `reachable_noOutsideDerived_of_right` : sur les états atteignables, le droit `Modify` sur la source (§63.1) implique la vérification de §63.4, qui ne rejette donc jamais un `transfer` à elle seule. La clause reste dans `TransferPre`. Le théorème figure dans la description de la PR.

**Point 4, Q3 : en cours.** Aujourd'hui, la disjonction n'est prouvée que pour l'entrée qu'on libère. Pour la confirmer sur toutes les entrées d'un pool vivant, un agent prouve un invariant noyau sur les états atteignables : aucune autorité active ne couvre une feuille de la place qui la détient. C'est exactement ce que maintiennent §63.8 et §65.3. Comme `internal` couvre exactement le stockage et que les entrées sont dans le stockage, les entrées seront alors disjointes des feuilles de la valeur du pool.

Une nuance sur « stockage possédé » : le contrat n'exige pas que la valeur du pool possède le stockage (§46 : stockage local, statique, alloué ou émis par une arène). Dans le témoin `hst`, par exemple, c'est la frame 0 qui possède le stockage. L'agent vérifie chaque témoin. Si la disjonction se prouve, il n'y aura pas à restreindre l'écriture.

content.text:
Les cinq points sont faits et prouvés en local. Le point 4 (Q3) est confirmé.

**Q3, point 4.** Sur les états atteignables, les entrées d'un pool vivant ne touchent jamais les feuilles de la valeur du pool : c'est `pool_entries_meta_disjoint`. Il n'y a donc rien à restreindre dans l'écriture des métadonnées. Le corollaire `freeSlot_keeps_entries` montre qu'un `freeSlot` accepté laisse l'état de toutes les entrées du pool inchangé.
- La preuve passe par un invariant noyau, prouvé dans le nouveau module `HolderCover` : aucune autorité active ne couvre une feuille de la place qui la détient. Il est maintenu par §63.8 et §65.3. Ce n'est pas une clause de §57.
- Comme `internal` couvre exactement le stockage et que les entrées sont dans le stockage, la disjonction en découle.
- Le théorème noyau suppose `DDSound`, une hypothèse normative (§80). C'est elle qui donne WF3 sur les états atteignables, et WF3 sert à borner les places détentrices lorsque `enter` et `alloc` ajoutent des places.

**« Stockage possédé ».** Le contrat n'exige pas que la valeur du pool possède le stockage (§46). Dans les témoins, le stockage est possédé par la frame 0 pour `w`, `x` et `c`, et par la valeur du pool pour `m`. La disjonction tient dans les deux cas, car elle ne repose pas sur la possession. La description de la PR le signale.

**Vérifications**
- Le build complet passe en 41 jobs, sans avertissement.
- La recherche de `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide` et `axiom` ne trouve rien.
- Le relevé des axiomes couvre 38 modules et 7 197 constantes. On n'y trouve que `propext`, `Quot.sound` et `Classical.choice`, ce dernier seulement dans `Statics` et `Rename/*`.

Une relecture indépendante de ce tour est en cours. Je commiterai, pousserai et mettrai à jour la description de la PR (tableau et points ouverts) à son retour. La PR reste en draft.

| 3. `KExt` | `K` est un paramètre (§48, §80), pas une définition concrète. `KExt` est donc documenté comme une obligation d'interface rattachée à §42, avec ses 13 théorèmes dépendants, tous dans la bisimulation de renommage. La relecture a confirmé que cette liste est complète. |

- Le relevé des axiomes porte sur 38 modules et 7 196 constantes, et ne donne rien en dehors de `propext`, `Quot.sound` et `Classical.choice`.
- La relecture indépendante n'a trouvé rien de bloquant dans le code. Pour suivre ses remarques, j'ai retiré `freeSlot_keeps_entries`, qui n'était pas demandé, et corrigé la description de la PR.

- Nothing outside the task was added.

Every finding needs evidence: a spec quote, a counterexample or command output. No evidence, no finding. Never ask for additions beyond the task.

## Summary

Reference formalization (Lean 4, `formal/`) of the ERN memory model, rebuilt on
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` after the arbitrations Q1–Q28 of the v0 blocking report and
their two follow-ups. `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` is unchanged.

Modules: `MemoryModel/Machine` (Part III), `MemoryModel/Access/*` (Parts IV–XIII, XV–XVI), `MemoryModel/Arena`
(Part XIV), `MemoryModel/Refinement` and `RefinementArena` (§82), `Lib/HandlePool` and `Lib/DataStack`
(non-normative library contracts), `Corpus/*` (test modules, imported by no model module).

## Spec v0.1 (commit `edbb7a3`, alone)

`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` is v0 with the header "Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate,
not yet validated" and the list of modified clauses: §36 (Q13), §40 (Q15), §47 (Q8), §51 and §60.1 (Q9/Q26),
§57 I5 (Q16), §59 (Q14), §63.4, §69.2 and §70.3 (Q9 and Q3 follow-ups: grounding exemption and kept-descendant
rule), §63.9 (Q1), §71.2 (Q24), §74 and §75 (B#45), §76.6 (Q2), §78.3 (Q7), §82.2 (Q18), §86 (Q6).

## Local contracts (non-normative)

**HandlePool v0.5** = HandlePool v0.4 annex D with:
- HP5-1 (Q3): `freeSlot` marks the entry free and increments its generation; no `endUse` effect, the kernel
  state is unchanged. Preconditions: administration right (live pool, `MetaRight`, §36), valid handle, no leaf
  of the entry `Init`.
- HP5-1' (Q3, second follow-up): no active strict descendant of this pool's `internal` covers the entry
  (replaces "derived from a companion"; covers §73 reanchoring onto `internal`). A pool nested in an entry
  blocks freeing that entry; the parent pool's authorities do not block the nested pool's `freeSlot`.
- HP5-1'' (Q5 extended to `freeSlot`): missing pool `reject`; invalid handle `fail` (a dead pool's handle is
  stale); then `reject` without the right; then `reject` on the content condition.
- HP5-2, HP5-3: the two mandatory proofs of Q3 (below).
- HP5-4 (Q4): D.2, D.3 and D.4 (3) per pool (the slot's pool); nested pools allowed.
- HP5-5 (Q5): handle validation precedes the right check in `resolve` and `resolveMany`: `fail`.
- HP5-6 (Q12): a handle of a free entry is stale: `fail`.
- HP5-7 (Q4): every library step is, on the kernel side, a sequence of accepted kernel steps O1–O16; the
  kernel guarantees hold on the whole state (`kernel_guarantee`).
- Retired with the v0.4 `freeSlot`: `pool_freeSlot_ends_content`, the content-end machinery and the v0.4
  literal D.2/D.4 refutation witnesses.

**DS-v2** = DS-v1 with:
- DS2-1 (Q11 d): `mark` requires `AdminRight`, else `reject`.
- DS2-2 (Q11 e): `grow` stores the new block authority into the place currently holding the block authority.
- DS2-3 (Q28 c): a dead stack invalidates its marks: `rewind` is `fail`.
- DS2-4 (DS-R1): "a cell above m" is every cell at a position `≥ m.top`.
- DS2-5 (DS-R4): `grow` with `extra = 0` is `ok` (in-place reissue of the same region).
- DS2-6 (DS-R3): `rewind` on a missing stack index is `fail`.
- DS-v1 items now decided: push without room `fail` (Q11 a); `grow` of a non-block `reject` (Q11 b); §76.5
  applies to `newStack` (Q11 c); dead or foreign mark `fail` before the right (Q11 f); §36 applies to `rewind`
  (Q27 a).

## Guarantees asked by the arbitration, on reachable states, without extra non-normative hypothesis

Hypotheses used: `DDSound` (§80) and `StaticsOK` (§47), both normative.
- Q1: `Access.reachable_kinv` (§57 on reachable states, transfer no longer excepted);
  `Access.reachable_cycle_rejected` (the v0 ownership-cycle run is rejected by §63.9). Auxiliaries `KAux` and
  `HeldAnchored` are proved initially and preserved by every step (`reachable_inv`).
- Q3 (1): `Lib.HandlePool.Witness.freeSlot_after_transfer`: from `PState.init`, `newPool`, `allocSlot`,
  `resolve` Modify, `write`, `transfer` to a local of the same shape (created by `enterFrame`), `unresolve`,
  `freeSlot` accepted, with `internal` derived.
- Q3 (2): `Lib.HandlePool.freeSlot_meta_write`: on every library-reachable state, for a pool with `AdminRight`,
  the kernel `write` of the pool value through the authority grounding `MetaRight` is accepted; its effect is the
  identity when the pool value's leaves are `Init`.
- Q7: `Arena.resetNoDeps_of_noCover` (§78.3 from §78.2 and I3), `Arena.reset_iff_derive_release` (`reset` iff
  `derive` then `release`, both directions, `ok` and `reject`).
- B#45: `Access.pin_unpinEff_iff` (`unpin` ends the designated obligation only), `Access.reachable_i5`,
  `Refinement.pinned_address_stable_reachable`, corpus case `Corpus.MM3H.B45`.

## Verdict changes (arbitration Q21)

| Case | Historical expected verdict | Justification | New verdict (v0.1) | Deciding clause | Obtained |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MM3-H H16 | ok ×4, then read `reject`; v0 obtained `reject` at the reception (case defect) | v0 §63.4 had no exemption: parameter 4 blocked | unchanged; class Spec 3 (Q21) | v0.1 §63.4 exemption; §66.1, §70 | ok ×4, read `reject` |
| MM3-H H21 | `ok` (material) | Jalon 3 draft accepted `issue` through a `writeShared` branch of `MetaRight` | `reject` at `issue` (= obtained) | §36, §77.1 | `reject`; twin with a `Modify` parameter `ok` |
| MM3-H H49 | to arbitrate; v0 obtained: cycle ok, `endUse` 2 and 3 ok, 7 and 8 exercisable in no mode, `reset` `reject` | NoLock not adopted (§65, §27); residual blocking allowed (§88) | regression test: cycle ok, 7 and 8 exercisable in no mode, `reset` `reject` (exempt from a twin, Q21), `endUse` 2 and 3 `reject` | v0.1 §69.2 last sentence (Q9 follow-up) for `endUse`; §78.2 for `reset` | same; twin without the cycle `ok` |
| MM3-H H50 transfer | to arbitrate; v0 obtained `reject` | self-transfer into the covered place left open | `reject` (= obtained) | §63.8, §88 | `reject`; twin `ok` |
| MM3-H H50 issue | to arbitrate; v0 obtained `reject` | issue into a leaf of the region left open | `reject` (= obtained) | §77.2, §88 | `reject`; twin `ok` |
| MM3-H H51 | to arbitrate; v0 obtained `reject` / `ok` | view on `v` stored in `v`'s owned storage left open | direct `store` `reject`; through a helper `ok`, then write, release of the view and `endUse` of `v` `reject`; exit `ok` (= obtained) | §43 case 4, §65.2, §65.5, §67.1, §62.2, §69.1, §88 | same; twins `ok` |
| MM3-H W3 | `reset` during the views `reject`, after `endUse` `ok`, reissue `ok`; v0 literal reading mismatch | material does not say which values hold the blocks | the variant (blocks in fields of the structure) is the case; verdicts unchanged | §78.2, §69, §77 | same |
| MM3-H B45 (new) | `ok` under v0 (per-leaf pin flags, reading B#45) | `unpin(f1)` cleared a flag also set by `pin(S)` | `transfer(f1, d)` `reject` | v0.1 §74, §75 (Q23 B#45) | `reject`; twin without `pin(S)` `ok` |
| MM2-H H01 twin | the twin read the new allocation unwritten | `ub` by §10 ¶5, §15.3, not by address reuse | the variant is the twin: write then read `ok` | §16 ¶2, §16 ¶5 | `ok` |
| MM2-H H10 | use of an access formed outside the source range | formation has no machine transition (§14 ¶4, open boundary) | the access leaves the allocation: `ub` | §15 ¶1, §16.2 | `ub`; twin `ok` |
| Lib H31a, stale handle ⟨0,1,7⟩ during a resolution | `reject` | active `Modify` companion blocks (annex D.2) | `fail` | HP5-5 (Q5), §89 | `fail`; Q19 multi-step twin (conjunct 5) `ok` |
| Lib `pool_free_entry_handle` | undetermined (v0 module: `fail`) | annex D.3 "un slot déjà libre…" | `fail` | HP5-6 (Q12), HP5-1'' | `fail`; twins `ok` |
| Lib `pool_dead`, `freeSlot` | `reject` | liveness checked with the right, before the handle | `fail` (`allocSlot` stays `reject`) | HP5-1'' (Q5 extended) | `fail` |
| Lib `pool_two_freeSlot_cross` continuation | `ok` (ended the content of a live slot of pool 0) | v0.4 exemption of `internal` ancestors | `reject` | HP5-1 (leaf 6 is `Init`) | `reject`; twin without the write `ok` |
| Lib `pool_freeSlot_derived_internal`, kernel `endUse` 7 | `reject` | v0 §69.2: `internal` 6 held outside the slot | `ok` | v0.1 §69.2 exemption | `ok` |
| Lib W1, `freeSlot` right after the fields are written | `ok` (ended the content) | annex D.3 | `reject`; revised run (value moved to a local first, Q21) all `ok` | HP5-1, HP5-1'; v0.1 §63.4 for the transfers | as expected |
| Lib W2 (variant is the case, Q21), move at `w2a` (view 12 released, column authority 11 active) | `reject` | v0 §63.4: 11 covers the field from outside | `ok` (re-evaluated as asked) | v0.1 §63.4: 11 grounds the right | `ok`; `reject` while 11 and 12 active, `ok` after both released |
| DataStack DS03, `grow` of the replaced block | none, to arbitrate | DS-v1 silent | `reject` | DS-v2 (Q11 b) | `reject` |
| DataStack DS05, `push` without room | none, to arbitrate | DS-v1 silent | `fail` | DS-v2 (Q11 a) | `fail` |

No case is left with an expected/obtained mismatch. Classified, not encoded, non-blocking: MM3-H section J,
MM23-H14 and H17 (Q20). Open boundaries, non-blocking (Q22): MM2-H H10 formation, H13a, H13b; MM23-H04, H09
(`exitRoots` retained as reference realization), H13.

## Checks

- `lake build` in `formal/`: 28 jobs, no warning.
- `grep -rnE '\b(sorry|admit|native_decide)\b|^\s*axiom\b' --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake .`: empty.
- `collectAxioms` over every constant of the 25 modules (6396 constants, 2980 theorems): nothing outside
  `propext` and `Quot.sound` (no `Classical.choice`).

## Open points for the spec and contract owner (non-blocking)

1. Spec v0.1, "Validation and Revision Procedure": the v0 sentence "This edition has been validated and
   acquires normative authority…" was copied unchanged and contradicts the v0.1 header. It is not in the
   amendment list, so it was left as is.
2. HP5-3: when a leaf of the pool value is `Moved` (reachable with `AdminRight`,
   `Witness.meta_write_not_identity`), the realizing `write` makes it `Init`, while `freeSlot` leaves the kernel
   state unchanged.
3. W2: under v0.1 §63.4 the variant can no longer express a row move by another party while the column view
   lives; a case revision may be wanted.
4. H49: the Q21 baseline (v0 obtained) had `endUse` 2 and 3 `ok`; the Q9 follow-up rule makes them `reject`.
   The case records the v0.1 verdict.
5. DS2-4 is not stricter than DS-R1 alternative B ("regions issued after m"): with DS2-5, a zero `grow` after
   `mark` reissues a region below `m.top` and `rewind m` accepts. Safe: the rewind returns only cells at or
   above `m.top`.
6. MM23-H16: the lowest-address rule for a region with a nonzero leaf is still the brief's decision for §82.3;
   v0.1 §82.2 decides only all-zero-size regions.

skills.content:
# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

- ub-mode: Follow the reduced principles when writing or changing code. Every change follows First Make it Work, then Then Make it Right, then Follow Practice. Use when the user runs /ub-mode or asks for the reduced principles.
- product-management:brainstorm: Brainstorm a product idea, problem space, or strategic question with a sharp thinking partner
- ponytail:ponytail: Lazy senior dev mode: the smallest change that fully solves the task, and a reply a busy human understands in one read. Use on any coding task (writing, fixing, refactoring, reviewing, choosing dependencies) and when the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "simplest solution", "yagni", or complains about over-engineering or bloat. Levels: lite, full (default), ultra.
- ponytail:ponytail-audit: Quality audit of a whole repo: bugs, security holes, what breaks under real load, risky code without tests, slow paths, and what to delete, merge or split. Ranked, each finding explained in plain English. One-shot report, changes nothing. Use for "audit this codebase", "review the whole repo", "find bloat", "what can I delete", /ponytail-audit.
- ponytail:ponytail-debt: List every `shortcut:` comment (and older `ponytail:` ones) as a debt ledger. One-shot report, changes nothing. Use for "ponytail debt", "what did ponytail defer", "list the shortcuts", /ponytail-debt.
- ponytail:ponytail-gain: Show ponytail's measured savings (code, cost, speed) from the benchmark. One-shot display. Use for /ponytail-gain, "what does ponytail save", "ponytail impact".
- ponytail:ponytail-help: Quick reference for ponytail levels, skills and commands. One-shot display. Use for /ponytail-help, "ponytail help", "how do I use ponytail".
- ponytail:ponytail-review: Quality review of a change: is the logic right, is it safe, does it hold under real load, is risky code tested, is it fast enough, and is every line needed. Reads the connected code, not only the diff. Each finding is explained in plain English. Use for "review this", "code review", "review the last commit", "review my PR", "is this over-engineered", /ponytail-review.

- Decide whether to offer, propose or start a session from this prompt, whether or not `start_session` is loaded yet. If it is only listed as a deferred tool and not loaded yet, load it first with `ToolSearch` (query "select:mcp__ccd_session__start_session", alone in its message); that load does not count as the turn's first message or first tool call.
